summary:
Map of the one-thread inversion call path in /home/user/mibz2 at HEAD 1a871bb (= origin/master; the local branch `master` is older, 2cc0829). Read-only: nothing built, run or written.

One function carries every block on the paths CI measures: `decode_block<I: bwt::InverseBwt>` (/home/user/mibz2/src/lib.rs:332). The kernel is a type parameter, not a config value: `Scratch<I = bwt::Segmented>` (lib.rs:278). `Segmented` is the default for `decode`, `decode_blocks`, `BzReader::new` and every `Plan::Workers(n)` worker, so it is also what CI's 2- and 4-thread rows run (CI runners have 2 physical cores, below `COOP_MIN_CORES` = 6).

The records route (#324) is a branch at the top of `decode_block` (lib.rs:341-362): `reads_runs() && runs::takes_runs(b)`, then `runs::front`, the `orig_ptr < n` check, `InverseBwt::invert_runs(&s.runs, n, b.orig_ptr, &mut s.ll, k)`, then `finish` (RLE1 and CRC). A block not admitted takes the column route (lib.rs:363-390).

The narrowest place for a cells try-and-fall-back is inside `Segmented::invert_runs` (/home/user/mibz2/src/bwt.rs:152-165), before `runs::fill` at line 160. It has the records, n, orig_ptr, the output Vec and the kernel's own state. No team path calls it. Its present body is the fallback, and that body clears `out` itself, so nothing needs undoing on refusal. Two constraints: the records are private to module `runs` with no accessor, and a refusal must not surface as `invert_runs == false`, because `decode_block` then hits `debug_assert!(false)` (lib.rs:361), a panic in test and fuzz builds.

No cargo feature, environment variable or builder option selects a kernel or route in src/ today. Routes are forced by the type parameter (`decode_with::<Plain>` against `::<Segmented>`), by `Kernels::scalar()`, by `Plan`/`with_plan`, and in tests by editing `Symbols.max_len` around the admission edge.

facts.fact: `pub trait InverseBwt: Default + Send`. Required: `fn invert(&mut self, ll: &[u8], counts: &[u32; 256], orig_ptr: u32, out: &mut Vec<u8>);`. Provided: `fn wants_checkpoints(&self) -> bool` (false); `fn invert_checkpointed(&mut self, ll: &[u8], counts: &[u32; 256], checkpoints: &[[u32; 256]], orig_ptr: u32, out: &mut Vec<u8>)`; `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "trace"))] fn buffers(&self) -> Vec<crate::trace::Buffer>`; `fn invert_in_place(&mut self, ll: &mut Vec<u8>, counts: &[u32; 256], orig_ptr: u32) -> bool` (false); `fn reads_runs(&self) -> bool` (false); `fn invert_runs(&mut self, r: &crate::runs::Runs, n: usize, orig_ptr: u32, out: &mut Vec<u8>, k: crate::Kernels) -> bool` (default body is `unreachable!("invert_runs on a kernel that doesn't read runs")`). Trait doc: 'Its buffers are its own, kept from block to block.' No trait or struct named `Kernels` chooses the inverse BWT: `Kernels` is the SIMD selector.

facts.topic: 1. How the decoder picks a kernel
facts.fact: By a generic type parameter only. `pub struct Scratch<I: bwt::InverseBwt = bwt::Segmented>` has private fields `ll: Vec<u8>, counts: [u32; 256], checkpoints: Vec<[u32; 256]>, inverse: I, rle: Vec<u8>, runs: runs::Runs`. `decode()` is `decode_with::<bwt::Segmented>(data, Kernels::detect())`. `decode_with<I>` builds `Scratch::<I>::default()`. `decode_blocks` hard-codes `Scratch::<bwt::Segmented>`. `BzReader::new` / `with_kernels` hold `scratch: Scratch` (the default parameter, so Segmented). No config value or cargo feature is involved.

`StreamDecoder::new(threads, slots, k)` takes the service core only when `!forced && threads == SERVICE_THREADS (10) && k.avx2 && k.clmul && service_target(..)`. Otherwise `Plan::for_threads(threads)` then `defaulted`. `plan_with` returns `Plan::Workers(threads)` when the topology is unreadable or `threads.min(phys) < COOP_MIN_CORES` (6). `planned` maps `Plan::Workers(n)` to `with_inverse::<Segmented>`, `Teams{k: 2|3|4}` to `with_inverse::<Cooperative<K>>`, any other team size to `Segmented` workers; `PIPELINED_PLAN` (3 teams of 3) goes to `pipelined_levers`. So on one thread, and on any machine under 6 physical cores (CI's runners), every worker runs `worker::<Segmented>` and calls `decode_block`.

`decode_block` and `Segmented` cannot tell one thread from N. The same `Segmented::invert_runs` runs under `decode`, `BzReader::new`, `decode_blocks` and each of N `Plan::Workers` workers. The CI bench's `mibz2` arm is `BzReader::new` at `threads == 1` and `BzReader::parallel(open()?, threads)` otherwise, at threads `1,2,$(nproc)`. So a change in `Segmented::invert_runs` is measured on all three thread rows. #324's journal says the same: 'CI's 4-CPU runners plan Workers(n) with Segmented at every thread count, so every bench row runs decode_block and sees the change.'

`stream::Scanner::next(&mut self, syms: Vec<u16>) -> Result<Event, Error>` calls `block::read_item(br: &mut Bits, level: u32, syms: Vec<u16>) -> Result<Item, (ErrorKind, Vec<u16>)>`. That yields `Event::Block { index, bit, end, stream, level, symbols: Symbols }`, with `pub struct Symbols { crc: u32, orig_ptr: u32, seq_to_unseq: [u8; 256], syms: Vec<u16>, eob: u16, max_len: usize }` and `max_len = 100_000 * level`. The `syms` Vec is passed in by value, reserved to `MAX_SYMS`, and handed back by the caller after the block (`syms = symbols.syms`). The stream's combined CRC is folded from the stored block CRCs in the scanner and checked at the stream's end marker, not in `decode_block`.

`pub fn decode_block<I: bwt::InverseBwt>(b: &block::Symbols, k: Kernels, s: &mut Scratch<I>, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<u32, ErrorKind>`. Steps: (1) `let cooperative = s.inverse.wants_checkpoints();` (2) `if s.inverse.reads_runs() && runs::takes_runs(b)`; (3) `let n = runs::front(b, &mut s.runs, k)?;` (4) `if b.orig_ptr as usize >= n { return Err(ErrorKind::BadOrigPtr); }` (5) trace mark InvertStart under `cfg(feature = "trace")`; (6) `let done = s.inverse.invert_runs(&s.runs, n, b.orig_ptr, &mut s.ll, k);` (7) trace mark InvertEnd; (8) `if done { return finish(&s.ll, b.crc, k, out); }` (9) `debug_assert!(false, "the run records don't tile the block");` then falls through to the column route. On this route `s.counts`, `s.checkpoints` and `s.rle` are not touched, and `s.ll` holds only the inversion's output.

`let n = mtf::mtf(b, &mut s.ll, &mut s.counts, k)?` (or `mtf::mtf_checkpoints(..)` when cooperative). Then `if b.orig_ptr as usize >= n { return Err(ErrorKind::BadOrigPtr) }`. Then `let in_place = !cooperative && s.inverse.invert_in_place(&mut s.ll, &s.counts, b.orig_ptr);`, else `invert_checkpointed(.., &mut s.rle)` or `invert(.., &mut s.rle)`. Then `finish(inverted, b.crc, k, out)` with `inverted = &s.ll` if in place, else `&s.rle`. `mtf` clears `ll` and reserves `b.max_len`: `pub fn mtf(b: &Symbols, ll: &mut Vec<u8>, counts: &mut [u32; 256], k: Kernels) -> Result<usize, ErrorKind>`.

`runs::fill(r, n, &mut self.tt, k)` builds the LF table `P[i] = L[i] | LF(i) << 8` into `self.tt.0: Vec<u32>` (cleared first, reserve n, or n + 8 with AVX2). Then `pub fn walk_back_room(tt: &mut TVector, orig_ptr: u32, out: &mut Vec<u8>, s: &mut SegScratch)`. If `tt.len() < MIN_SEGMENTED` (`1 << 16`) it runs `walk_back(tt, orig_ptr, out)`, which does `out.clear(); out.resize(n, 0)`, writes from the end, then `repeat_cycle(out, m)`. Otherwise it runs `room_segments::<FLAGGED_LANES, PREFETCH, true>(tt, orig_ptr, s, FLAGGED_SEGMENTS)` (32 lanes, PF_L1, 512 segments) and then `s.assemble_reversed(out)`, which does `out.clear(); out.reserve(n)`, writes spare capacity from the end, `repeat_cycle`, and `unsafe { out.set_len(n) }`.

facts.topic: 2. What the inversion's out must hold
facts.fact: Trait contract: the block's RLE1-coded text 'into `out` (cleared): exactly what `invert` gives for the block's column'. That is exactly n bytes in forward order (first to last), `out.len() == n`, with no slack needed after it, equal to `bwt::walk`: the first n steps of Ψ from `orig_ptr`, the primary index's cycle repeated and cut at n if it is shorter than n. On the records route `out` is `s.ll` (the worker's `Scratch`, reused block to block). The consumer is `finish(inverted: &[u8], ..)`, which takes a plain slice. The whole block must be complete and contiguous before RLE1 starts: there is no streaming seam between the inversion and RLE1/CRC.

Both run after the inversion, in `fn finish(inverted: &[u8], stored: u32, k: Kernels, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<u32, ErrorKind>`. It takes `let start = out.len();`, then `rle::unrle(inverted, out, k)` appends to the caller's `out` (on Err it does `out.truncate(start)` and returns the kind). Then `crc::crc32(&out[start..], k)` over the whole decoded block; a mismatch truncates and returns `ErrorKind::BlockCrc { stored, computed }`. `pub fn unrle(rle: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>, k: Kernels) -> Result<(), ErrorKind>` reserves `n + 64` (AVX2) or n on `out`; its AVX2 loop reads only while `i + 35 <= n`, so the inverted slice needs no trailing slack. `pub fn crc32(data: &[u8], k: Kernels) -> u32`.

`decode_with` keeps one `out: Vec<u8>` for the whole file and `decode_block` appends each block. `BzReader` sequential (`Seq::read`) clears `self.out` before each block. The parallel `worker` pops a Vec from `st.free_out`, clears it, and wraps `decode_block` in `catch_unwind`; on a panic it sets `scratch = Scratch::default()` and reports `ErrorKind::Internal`. The sequential paths (`decode_with`, `decode_blocks`, `Seq::read`) have no `catch_unwind`: a panic in a kernel reaches the caller.

A record is `u16 = (byte as u16) << 8 | length`, with length 1..=127: `const CAP: u32 = 127;` and 'A record's longest run: a longer run is cut into records of at most this many rows'. The scalar front writes `runs.push((c as u16) << 8 | len as u16)` with `len = left.min(CAP)`. The AVX2 front writes the low byte as the length and the high byte as the byte (`*(out as *mut u8) = total as u8; *(out as *mut u8).add(1) = c as u8`), and `long!` writes `(c << 8 | len) as u16`. The records are in L (row) order. Adjacent records share a byte where a run over 127 rows was cut. Readers decode `(x >> 8) as usize` and `(x & 0xff) as u32`, so `fill` would structurally accept lengths up to 255.

`pub struct Runs { runs: Vec<u16>, counts: [u32; 256], per: [u32; 256], lit: Vec<u64>, one: Vec<u64> }`. All five fields are private to module `runs`. `counts` is each byte's rows, `per` each byte's records, `lit`/`one` the AVX2 front's symbol bitmaps. Methods: `impl Default`; `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "trace"))] pub fn buffers(&self) -> Vec<crate::trace::Buffer>` (names "runs.runs", "runs.lit", "runs.one"); `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn of_column(ll: &[u8]) -> Runs`; `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn records_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Vec<u16>`. There is no non-test accessor for the records, their count or the counts: not found. The count of maximal runs (the journal's r) is not stored: `runs.len()` and the sum of `per` count records after the 127 cut.

`pub fn front(b: &Symbols, r: &mut Runs, k: Kernels) -> Result<usize, ErrorKind>` returns '`mtf::mtf`'s length, or its error, with no column written'. It dispatches to `unsafe fn front_avx2(b: &Symbols, f: &mut Runs) -> Option<usize>` when `front_fast(k)` (k.avx2 plus bmi2, lzcnt and popcnt detected); on `None` or otherwise it runs `pub fn front_scalar(b: &Symbols, r: &mut Runs) -> Result<usize, ErrorKind>`. Errors: `RunTooLong` (weight >= `MAX_RUN_WEIGHT` = 2*1024*1024) and `BlockTooLong` (n + run > max_len, or a literal at n >= max_len). `front_avx2` returns None when `b.max_len >= 1 << 31 || m >= 1 << 24`, when there is no EOB, for 22 or more run symbols together, and on a length overflow; the scalar loop then decides.

`pub fn fill(r: &Runs, n: usize, tt: &mut TVector, k: Kernels) -> bool`. It does `tt.0.clear()` first. It returns false, with `tt` left empty, if `n >= 1 << 24`, if the counts do not sum to n, or if a record has `len == 0 || len > n - q || len > lim[c] - next[c]`, or `q != n` at the end. It dispatches to `fill_avx2` (reserve n + 8, 8 entries a store, `set_len(n)`) when `k.avx2`, else `fill_scalar`. On success every link in the table is below n, which the walks' unchecked reads rely on.

`pub fn takes_runs(b: &Symbols) -> bool`. With `let syms = &b.syms;` it returns false if `b.max_len >= 1 << 24 || 2 * syms.len() > b.max_len`. Otherwise it counts run symbols (`s <= 1`) in a sample: the whole block if `syms.len() <= WINDOW * WINDOWS` (64 * 64 = 4096), else 64 windows of 64 symbols at `i * step` with `step = syms.len() / WINDOWS`. It returns `RUN_SHARE * runs >= seen` with `RUN_SHARE = 32`. It reads only `Symbols` (the bound, not the length) and runs before any front. The second condition was added by #353 (c9329f0).

facts.topic: 3. Where orig_ptr and n come from; a block not admitted
facts.fact: `orig_ptr` is `br.bits(24)` from the block header, refused at read time if `orig_ptr as usize > 10 + max_len` (BadOrigPtr), and carried as `Symbols.orig_ptr: u32`. `n` is the `Ok` value of `runs::front` (records route) or `mtf::mtf` (column route). A block for which `reads_runs()` or `takes_runs(b)` is false never calls `front`: it takes lib.rs:363-390 (`mtf::mtf`, the orig_ptr check, `Segmented::invert_in_place` = `build` + `walk_segments_room` over `ll`, `finish`).

Inside `Segmented::invert_runs`, before `if !crate::runs::fill(r, n, &mut self.tt, k)` at bwt.rs:160. In scope there: `r: &crate::runs::Runs`, `n: usize`, `orig_ptr: u32` (already checked `< n` by the caller), `out: &mut Vec<u8>` (= `s.ll`), `k: crate::Kernels`, and `&mut self` (`tt`, `seg`, and any buffers added to `Segmented`). Lines 160-164 unchanged are today's route. Nothing else calls this method: `Cooperative::invert_runs` has its own body, and the pipelined and service teams use `front_stage` and `Front::invert_alone`.

facts.topic: 4. Alternative branch point and why it is wider
facts.fact: `decode_block` lib.rs:353, between `runs::front` and `invert_runs`, is generic over `I`. It also runs for `Cooperative<K>` workers (`Plan::Teams{k: 2|3|4}`) and has only `s.inverse: I` to call through, so a branch there needs a new trait method or a type test. The existing false-return path there is not a usable refusal: it executes `debug_assert!(false, "the run records don't tile the block")`, then re-runs the whole front as `mtf::mtf` for the column route.

facts.topic: 4. Access to the records from the branch point
facts.fact: `bwt.rs` cannot read `r.runs`, `r.counts` or `r.per` (private fields of `runs::Runs`). Every present consumer is a function inside src/runs.rs taking `&Runs` (`fill`, `cuts`, `cuts_tile`, `fill_share`) or the child module src/runs/tests.rs. The example says so: 'The decoder's own records are private to `runs::Runs`, so the cells kernel is fed these: the same records, made here from the column', and its `Kernel::slots(&mut self, n: usize, recs: &[u16], p: u32)` takes a bare `&[u16]`.

None is required by the present fallback. (a) `out` (`s.ll`): both fallback writers clear it first (`walk_back`: `out.clear(); out.resize(n, 0)`; `assemble_reversed`: `out.clear(); out.reserve(n)`), and the column route's `mtf` clears `ll` too, so only its capacity persists. (b) `self.tt`: `fill` starts with `tt.0.clear()`. (c) `self.seg`: `room_segments` rebuilds `starts`, `bufs[..ns]`, `next` and sets `s.first`, `s.n` on every call; `walk_back` (blocks under 2^16 rows) does not touch `seg`. (d) `r` is a shared borrow, so the records cannot be changed in `invert_runs`. (e) `Scratch.counts`, `checkpoints` and `rle` are untouched on the records route. (f) The trace marks InvertStart/InvertEnd wrap the whole `invert_runs` call, so a try plus fallback is one span. The time spent before a refusal is not recoverable.

facts.topic: 4. The example kernel's interface to the seam
facts.fact: `fn slots(&mut self, n: usize, recs: &[u16], p: u32)`; `fn induce_cells<const COUNT: bool>(&mut self) -> (u32, u32, u64)` (the cycle's word, its length with the mark, cells); `fn write_cells(&mut self, word: u32, len: u32, n: usize, out: &mut Vec<u8>)`. `write_cells` does `out.resize(n + 32, 0)` at entry and `out.truncate(n)` at exit, and repeats a cycle shorter than the block, so it leaves `out.len() == n` in forward order but needs capacity n + 32. `slots` allocates one buffer of `total = lay.rules + 16 * (n + 4)` bytes with `cap = (2 * n + 8) * SLOT` (SLOT = 24) for each of two orders, about 128 n bytes (about 115 MB of zeroed virtual memory at n = 900,000), re-allocated only when `self.buf.len() < total`. No cell budget or early stop exists in `induce_cells`: not found. No r/n test exists in the example's kernel: not found.

In `read_item`: block magic, the randomised bit, `orig_ptr > 10 + max_len` (BadOrigPtr), `n_in_use == 0` (NoSymbols), groups 2..=6, selectors >= 1, code lengths 1..=20, Huffman codes, SelectorOverrun, Truncated. In the front (`runs::front` or `mtf::mtf`, same errors): `RunTooLong`, `BlockTooLong`. In `decode_block`: `b.orig_ptr as usize >= n` gives `BadOrigPtr` on both routes, after the front's own error, so n >= 1 at the inversion. In `fill`: the tiling (false means a bug in the front, not an input error). Nothing checks that the column is a BWT image or that LF is one cycle.

facts.topic: 5. A column that is not a BWT
facts.fact: The walks are defined on any table whose links are below n. `walk` gives the first n steps from `orig_ptr`, going round its cycle again if the cycle is shorter than n. The backward route is made byte-identical by `repeat_cycle<T: Copy>(out: &mut [T], m: usize)`: 'This makes the backward walk exactly `walk` on any table, so a corrupt block's error is the same too.' The join in `assemble_reversed` stops when it returns to its first segment, and `walk_back` breaks when `i == orig_ptr`. The bytes then decide the error: `RunUnfinished` from `unrle`, or `BlockCrc { stored, computed }` whose `computed` field is compared by tests (`assert!(ra == rc, ..)`) and by the fuzz's `res != plain_res`. Crafted non-BWT columns (random permutations, periodic columns of several cycles, any primary index) are tested against libbzip2 in `crafted_blocks_match_libbzip2`.

facts.topic: 5. Panics and assertions on the one-thread path
facts.fact: lib.rs:361 `debug_assert!(false, "the run records don't tile the block")`. bwt.rs:98 `unreachable!` (default `invert_runs`). bwt.rs:769 `assert!(at < n || n == 0)` (`assemble_reversed`). bwt.rs:1268 `const { assert!(L <= 64) }`. bwt.rs:1272-1275 `assert!(n <= 1 << 23, "the room walk takes at most 2^23 rows, not {n}")`. bwt.rs:1279 `assert!((orig_ptr as usize) < n, "the primary index past the block")` (BACK). bwt.rs:1370-1371, :1387, :1548 are `debug_assert!`s in the room walk. `walk_back` uses checked indexing (`t[i]`, `out[n - 1 - k]`), as does `walk` (`t[orig_ptr as usize]`, bwt.rs:663). bwt.rs:546 is `try_into().unwrap()` in `run_joins` (column build). `[profile.fuzz]` sets `debug-assertions = true` and `overflow-checks = true`, so in the fuzz a debug assertion is a counted failure. `[profile.test]` sets `opt-level = 3`.

facts.topic: 5. The example kernel's own assertions (for comparison)
facts.fact: `slots` asserts `total < u32::MAX as usize && n < MARK as usize && (p as usize) < n` and `row as usize == n && !empty` ("the records do not tile the block"). `induce_cells` asserts `rr >= 1 && self.buf.len() >= lay.rules + 80` ("`slots` has not run"). The rest is `unsafe` raw-offset reads and writes (`rd64`/`wr64`, `get_unchecked`) with SAFETY comments. The example is checked against `bwt::walk` on arbitrary columns by `rauzy --arbitrary` (`fn arbitrary(cases: usize)`).

facts.topic: 6. How tests and benches force a route today
facts.fact: Column route always: `Scratch::<Plain>` / `decode_with::<bwt::Plain>` (benches/decode.rs 'plain walk 1t'; tests/decode.rs:155; tests/in_place.rs). Records route where admitted: `Scratch::<Segmented>` / `decode_with::<Segmented>` (tests/common `ours` and `Mibz2`). The admission edge is forced by setting `b.max_len` to `1 << 20`, `2 * b.syms.len()` or one less. Which route ran is detected by a sentinel record `const UNTOUCHED: u16 = 0xffff` planted in `s.runs.runs` (private fields reached from the child test module). Kernel sets by `fn kernels()` (scalar, plus detect where it differs). tests/admission.rs calls the public `mibz2::runs::takes_runs` on scanned blocks of real compressed data. The fuzz's classic candidates are `decode_with::<Segmented>` on scalar and detected kernels and the parallel decoder at 3 threads; classic mode has no route counter.

facts.topic: 6. What the CI bench and its stage table run
facts.fact: The PR bench builds default features (`cargo build --release --example ab --example windows --example phases`) and runs arms `mibz2,mibz2@base/ab` at threads `1,2,$(nproc)` with `--spread`. The stage table (examples/phases.rs) times `mtf::mtf`, `build`, `walk_segments_room_parts`, `seg.assemble`, `rle::unrle` and `crc::crc32`: the column route only. It does not run `runs::front`, `runs::fill` or `walk_back_room`. #324's journal notes this: '`examples/phases.rs`, which can't see this change'.

`cargo test` (test.yml:27) and `cargo miri test --lib -- miri_` (miri.yml:65) run default features only; clippy runs `--all-features` (test.yml:25). Feature-specific test jobs exist as precedent: occupancy.yml:71 (`--features trace`) and walk-stats.yml:44-49 (`--features walk-stats`). Miri's path filter covers `src/bwt.rs`, `src/coop.rs`, `src/parallel.rs`, `src/parallel/**`, `src/read.rs`, `src/runs.rs`, `src/runs/**`; it does not list `src/lib.rs`. Miri selects unit tests by the name prefix `miri_`.

Four points. (1) Kernel type, in `StreamDecoder::planned`: `Plan::Teams{k: 2|3|4}` gives `worker::<Cooperative<K>>`, which still calls `decode_block` but lands in `Cooperative::invert_runs` / `invert_checkpointed` (own bodies; they call the free functions `runs::fill`, `runs::cuts`, `walk_back_room`, `coop::build_runs`, `coop::walk_room_back`). (2) The pipelined teams (`PIPELINED_PLAN`, `pipelined_worker`) never call `decode_block` or the trait: they use `fn front_stage(b, f: &mut Front, k) -> Result<usize, ErrorKind>` (which calls `runs::takes_runs`, `runs::front`, `runs::cuts`), `Front::invert_alone` (`runs::fill` + `bwt::walk_back_room_parts`, or `build` + `walk_segments_room_parts`), `coop::invert_pipelined_from` and `finish_block`. (3) The service core (`service_worker`, `prepare`, `team_worker`) uses the same `front_stage`, `invert_alone` and `coop::invert_team_from`. (4) `coop::Source::Runs` has its own `runs::fill` fallback. Consequence: a change inside the body of `Segmented::invert_runs` reaches no team path. A change to `runs::takes_runs`, `runs::front`, `runs::fill`, `walk_back_room`, `room_segments` or `decode_block`'s shared lines reaches the teams too.

risks: A cells refusal must not be reported as `invert_runs` returning false. `decode_block` then executes `debug_assert!(false, "the run records don't tile the block")` (/home/user/mibz2/src/lib.rs:361), a panic in `cargo test` and on the fuzz profile (`debug-assertions = true`, /home/user/mibz2/Cargo.toml:80). In release it silently re-runs the whole front as `mtf::mtf` and takes the column route, which is not today's route for an admitted block.

`Segmented` is not a one-thread-only kernel. It is every `Plan::Workers(n)` worker's kernel (/home/user/mibz2/src/parallel.rs:218) and `decode_blocks`' (/home/user/mibz2/src/lib.rs:501). A branch in `Segmented::invert_runs` changes CI's 2- and 4-thread rows too, and puts one cells buffer in every worker's `Scratch`.

The example's buffer is about 128 n bytes a kernel (`(2 * n + 8) * 24` for each of two orders, plus 16 n arena and 16 n rules; /home/user/mibz2/examples/rauzy.rs:894-905), about 115 MB virtual at 900,000 rows, a worker. The policy's rule 4 caps peak RSS growth at 10% a corpus unless justified (/home/user/mibz2/docs/team/PERFORMANCE-POLICY.md, section 2). #324 alone added 4-10% on wikidata and text at 2-4 threads.

#324's confirmed harm was on `random` and `records`, whose blocks ran none of the new code. The journal's hypothesis (not a finding) is `Scratch`'s inline growth moving `counts` against `mtf_avx2`'s stack frame (/home/user/mibz2/docs/journal/2026-11-10-run-front-production.md:571-590). New inline state in `Segmented` or `Scratch` (the example's `Kernel` holds 16 Vecs plus a `Layout`) can move the column route's layout again, even though admission keeps those blocks on their old route.

Byte-identity on corrupt input rides on the exact inverted bytes. `BlockCrc { stored, computed }` and `RunUnfinished` are compared exactly by the differential tests and the fuzz (/home/user/mibz2/src/runs/tests.rs:532; /home/user/mibz2/examples/fuzz.rs:412). A cells route that differs from `bwt::walk` on a column that is not a BWT (several cycles, or a cycle shorter than n) changes the error. The example covers this with `rauzy --arbitrary`, but no src/ test does yet.

The records are private (`Runs.runs`, `counts`, `per`; /home/user/mibz2/src/runs.rs:87-96). The kernel must either live in module `runs` or get a new accessor. Any new method on `Runs` or change to `runs.rs` free functions is shared with the team paths (`front_stage`, `Cooperative::invert_runs`, `coop::RunsBuild`).

The sequential entry points have no `catch_unwind` (/home/user/mibz2/src/lib.rs:449-472; /home/user/mibz2/src/read.rs:294). An `assert!` in the cells kernel that fires in production (the example has three: rauzy.rs:902, :931, :1036) would panic the caller's thread in `decode` and `BzReader::new`; in the parallel worker it becomes `ErrorKind::Internal`.

The example's `write_cells` does `out.resize(n + 32, 0)` and relies on `out` keeping its length between blocks ('only the slack is written here', /home/user/mibz2/examples/rauzy.rs:1190-1191). In production `s.ll` is cleared or truncated by other routes between blocks, so that resize would zero-fill n + 32 bytes on each call, and `ll`'s capacity changes from today's.
The bench's stage table (examples/phases.rs) runs only the column route, so it cannot show the cells stages or their fallback cost. Only the whole-decoder rows can.

A feature-off first PR would be invisible to the gates named in the assignment: the CI bench builds default features (/home/user/mibz2/.github/workflows/bench.yml:143), and `cargo test` and Miri run default features (/home/user/mibz2/.github/workflows/test.yml:27, miri.yml:65). Its tests, Miri and fuzz reach would need their own steps, as walk-stats.yml and occupancy.yml do for their features.

`room_segments` asserts `n <= 1 << 23` (/home/user/mibz2/src/bwt.rs:1272), while `takes_runs` and `fill` admit up to 2^24. Unreachable from a real stream (`max_len <= 900,000`) but reachable from a hand-built `Symbols`, as the unit tests build them.

The trace ledger has no entries for the records' buffers (no "runs." name in /home/user/mibz2/src/trace.rs). `ledger_matches_a_workers_buffers` asserts every listed buffer has a ledger entry (trace.rs:839-841) and passes only because its blocks take the column route. A cells buffer listed in `Segmented::buffers()` with non-zero capacity in that test would fail it.
open_questions: Does 'the one-thread Segmented kernel' mean the kernel type `Segmented` wherever it runs (including CI's 2- and 4-thread `Plan::Workers` rows), or literally one decoding thread? The code has no signal for the latter at `decode_block` or `invert_runs`.

What is r for the 'free r/n test'? `Runs` holds the count of records after the 127-row cut (`runs.len()`, the sum of `per`), not the count of maximal runs. The journal's thresholds (r/n < 0.09 or 0.10) are stated on runs and give 0.0778 records against 0.0722 letters a row on Wikidata (/home/user/mibz2/docs/journal/monodromy/2026-11-10-rauzy-veech.md:961-963).

Where should the r/n test sit: in `decode_block` beside `takes_runs` (needs a `Runs` accessor and a trait hook, and is generic over the kernel), or inside `Segmented::invert_runs` (invisible to the admission tests that only see `takes_runs`)? The second keeps `decode_block` and the team paths untouched.

The cells budget is not in the example: `induce_cells` has no early stop. What does a mid-induction refusal return, and is the one-buffer state then safe to reuse on the next block? `slots` re-initialises both orders each block, but this needs the kernel map to confirm.

Should the kernel's buffer live inline in `Segmented`, or boxed or lazily allocated so that `Scratch<Segmented>`'s layout for the column route stays as on master? #324's journal proposed boxing `Runs` for that reason (run-front-production.md:602-604); it was not done, and `Scratch.runs` is still inline (/home/user/mibz2/src/lib.rs:291).

How should the reach of a forced cells route be counted in the fuzz? The #359 pattern recomputes the route outside the decoder as a function of the block alone. A budget refusal depends on the induction, not only on the block's symbols, so it needs either a public predicate or a counter exposed by the kernel; no such counter exists in src/ today outside the `wait-stats` and `walk-stats` features.

If the fuzz is to force the route (bypassing admission), what forces it? No runtime switch exists; the only precedents are a distinct kernel type parameter (as `Plain` against `Segmented`) and the doc(hidden) thread-local `with_plan`.
Does a new source file for the kernel need adding to the Miri workflow's path filters (as #324 added `src/runs.rs` and `src/runs/**`)? `src/lib.rs` is not in that filter today.
